desk.headline: Adjusted EPS $4.68 vs $2.78, beat; revenue up 24% to $9.5bn; 2026 guidance reaffirmed, 2027 outlook set

other.label: Free cash flow before growth investments

results: Revenue rose 24% to $9.5bn and adjusted EPS jumped to $4.68 from $2.78, helped by the power plants and CPower bought from LS Power in January.
Adjusted EBITDA reached $2.01bn: East up $507m on the new assets and higher capacity prices, Texas up $211m on retail margins and hot weather, Vivint up $39m.
GAAP net income was $561m vs $152m, despite a $155m non-cash loss on hedges as gas prices fell.
Agreed to sell six gas plants (4.9 GW) to LS Power for $4bn, closing expected in Q2 2027; $977m of shares bought back through October.
Liquidity fell to $6.0bn from $9.6bn at year-end after funding the acquisition; long-term debt is $21.8bn.

guidance.summary: NRG kept all 2026 ranges and set first 2027 ranges, which exclude the plant sale. It plans $3bn of buybacks across 2026–27 and an 8% dividend rise to $2.05 a share in 2027.

points: Management cast the $4bn plant sale as a value call after an unsolicited offer, not a change of strategy; the PJM fleet and CPower stay.
Sale proceeds go to extra buybacks and debt reduction, and it kept its long-term target of about 14% yearly growth in adjusted EPS and free cash flow to 2030.
It expects a definitive deal on its 1.2 GW Texas data centre power project by year-end.
Weak Texas wholesale prices are a 2027 headwind, partly offset by higher PJM prices; higher RGGI carbon costs also weigh.
Management indicated 2026 may land slightly below the middle of its guidance range.
call.source: NRG Energy, Inc. Q3 2026 Earnings Call Summary — Yahoo Finance, 9 Nov 2026
